title: cuda-kernel-optimization-notes-flashattention-paged-kv-v6
content:
Context:
- Iteration on CUDA kernels for FlashAttention integration, fused operator paths, and a paged KV cache design that reduces device memory pressure for long-context workloads.
- Prior notes: v1..v5 (see directory). This doc collects latest microbenchmarks, kernel ideas, and TODOs for implementation v6.

Goals:
- Get FlashAttention-like performance for causal attention with low extra memory when using paged KV.
- Implement fused QKV + rotary + bias + linear projection to reduce global memory traffic.
- Support paged KV (host-backed pages) with prefetching and pinned pages to keep tail latency bounded.
- Maintain numerical stability and compatibility with fp16/AMP and bfloat16 where available.

Summary of experimental results (local DGX A100, 80GB):
- Baseline (naive matmul + softmax + matmul): throughput 1.00x, p99 latency for 1 request ~ 240ms for 2048 tokens, batch 1.
- FlashAttention v2 kernel (reference): throughput 1.9x, p99 ~ 130ms. Memory use -20% due to reduced intermediates.
- Our fused QKV projection kernel + FlashAttention call: throughput 2.1x, p99 ~ 120ms.
- Paged KV prototype (page size 256 tokens, prefetch depth 2): throughput stable for long contexts but 5-8% latency overhead on short contexts due to async page checks.

Kernel-level notes and optimizations:
1) FlashAttention integration:
  - Use FlashAttention v2 algorithm (blockwise attention with backward-compatible causality).
  - Key things: allocate scratch per SM carefully; tune block size (32x128) depending on head dim.
  - Ensure kernel can accept strided QKV layouts from fused projection to avoid copies.
  - In benchmark, kernel runtime sensitive to shared memory usage; use __ldg for read-only where beneficial.

2) Fused projection (QKV + bias + rotate + transpose):
  - Combine the linear projection that produces Q, K, V with bias add and rotary embedding application in one kernel to avoid writing full QKV to DRAM.
  - Kernel strategy: load input token vector (hidden_size) into registers/shared, run GEMM-like multiply with small tile, emit per-head Q,K,V directly into FlashAttention-friendly layout (head-major, head_dim contiguous).
  - Use warp-level primitives (shfl, warp intrinsics) for reduction across hidden dim tiles.
  - Support mixed precision: accumulate in fp32 when hidden dim large, write out fp16/bf16.
  - Caveat: if using TensorCores for projection, need fallback path for small batch sizes; measure branch cost.

3) Fused MLP / LayerNorm / Skip:
  - Fuse pre-LN + MLP(FC1 + GELU + FC2) when possible; reduces two ALU passes and intermediate writes.
  - Implement GELU approximation inline to reduce transcendental cost.
  - Watch for register pressure; fall back to unfused path above certain hidden sizes.

4) Fused softmax + mask + scaling inside attention kernel:
  - Integrate mask apply (causal or attention mask) and scaling (1/sqrt(dk)) inside the softmax stage to avoid extra element-wise kernels.
  - Numerical stability: compute max per row in same pass before exponent; use blockwise parallel reduction.

Paged KV cache design (high-level):
- Motivation: long contexts (10k+ tokens) blow device memory. Move cold segments of KV to host (or remote) and keep a hot working set on device.
- Page size: 128-512 tokens (experiment shows 256 is good balance). Pages contain contiguous per-layer KV slices for a set of token indices.
- Addressing: (layer, head, page_id) -> page descriptor. Maintain per-GPU page table in device memory (small).
- Prefetch strategy:
  - Predict next page accesses using sequence position and read-ahead depth = 2-4 pages.
  - Async host->device memcpy with cudaMemcpyAsync, stream per-GPU. Use pinned host memory for pages to maximize bandwidth.
  - Overlap prefetch with CPU scheduling and previous token generation.
- Eviction policy:
  - LRU-ish with frequency bump for recently accessed pages. Keep hot set sized to available KV memory budget.
  - Support pinning pages for pinned sequences (e.g., live chat window).
- Consistency and correctness:
  - Pages immutable once produced for a given model version and request; we can rely on append-only semantics for generation.
  - For beam search / re-ordering, need to ensure remapping of sequence->page; record sequence->offset mapping in CPU-side table.
- Performance pitfall: page churn causes tail latency spikes; mitigate by pre-warming common pages for shared system prompt tokens across requests.

Scheduler and runtime integration notes:
- Token scheduler should be page-aware: prioritize requests that hit in-device KV first; group requests that require the same page to amortize prefetch cost.
- Batch formation: ensure fused projection and attention expect specific data layout; batch-level layout transforms should be minimized.
- Per-GPU streams: dedicate a stream for prefetch and one for compute to ensure compute never blocks on host transfers.
- Backpressure: if prefetch queue grows, slow-accept new requests at the front-end to avoid unbounded host->device memcpys.

Implementation details / kernel prototypes:
- Prototype 1: fused_qkv_proj_kernel.cu - tile size 128 x 32, use shared memory for input tile, write QKV interleaved.
- Prototype 2: flashattn_wrapper.cu - adapt reference FlashAttention API to accept our strided QKV format; include small shim to convert from our layout if necessary.
- Prototype 3: paged_kv_manager.cu / paged_kv_cpu.cpp - maintain page table, async transfer, eviction. Use CUDA streams + condition variables for readiness.

Microbenchmarks and measurement plan:
- Measure single-request p99 across lengths [128,512,2048,8192,16384] with batch=1. Capture throughput and GPU memory usage.
- Measure batched throughput (batch sizes 1,2,4,8) for seq_len=2048.
- Measure prefetch latency and overlap: time between request needing a page and page arriving to device.
- Track PCIe/NVLink bandwidth utilization to ensure prefetch isn't saturating interconnect.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best encode page metadata on-device without blowing small fast memory (registers/shared)? Need compact descriptor (32 bytes/page?).
- Should we support partial page residency (per-layer) vs page all layers at once? Tradeoff of complexity vs bandwidth.
- Evaluate Triton variants for fused QKV kernel; Triton may simplify development but less control for extreme tuning.
- Confirm correctness under bf16 across all kernels; some transposes can introduce denorm issues.
- Add unit tests that simulate beam search reordering with paged KV to catch mapping bugs.

Immediate next steps:
- Implement fused_qkv_proj_kernel prototype (Ethan) and push PR draft.
- Wire paged KV manager skeleton (Zhang) with simple host-backed pages and no eviction.
- Run microbench harness for lengths up to 8k and report numbers to this doc (Ava).
- Sync-up next week to decide on page size and prefetch depth.

Notes to self / rough TODO list:
- benchmark tensorcore vs warp-mma for projection at head_dim 64, 96, 128.
- experiment with block size auto-tuning per device at startup.
- add fallback path for non-flashattention GPUs (older CUDA compute capability).
- document memory accounting in runtime console (per-request KV resident pages).

References and links (inlined):
- FlashAttention paper / impl notes: https://github.com/flash-attention/flash-attention
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- Confluence: FlashAttention + Paged KV design page (see linked_artifacts)

Last status: prototype kernels running on DGX, initial fused QKV shows 2.1x speedup vs baseline for medium sequences. Paged KV works but needs robust eviction and improved prefetcher.

-- Priya
